newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysians protest remarks by Singapore's Lee.
newsitem.headline: Malaysians protest remarks by Singapore's Lee.

text.p: About 100 members of Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's political party on Thursday demonstrated against Singapore senior minister Lee Kuan Yew for remarks he made criticising Johor state, witnesses said.
Carrying placards that denounced Lee, the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) members demonstrated outside the Senai airport in Johor while awaiting the arrival of Mahathir.
It was the first public demonstration against Lee by Malaysians since Wednesday when he said Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings".

Mahathir is making a one-day official visit to the state, which is just across a short causeway from Singapore. He was scheduled to meet local UMNO members, witness a corporate signing ceremony and launch an internet homepage at a resort.

A Reuters photographer at the Johor airport, David Loh, said the demonstrators carried placards with words in Malay such as "Johor Demands Your Apology", "Pull Back Your Statement Kuan Yew" and "Lee Kuan Yew Destroyer of ASEAN Unity".
Both Malaysia and Singapore are members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, along with Brunei, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam and the Philippines.
Public criticism or demonstrations against fellow ASEAN members are rare.
Mahathir arrived at around 0900 local time (0100 GMT) and smiled and waved at the crowd.

Lee came under fire from Malaysian politicians on Wednesday after local newspapers reported that Lee described Johor as "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings" in a court affidavit filed in a Singapore court on January 27.
Lee's affidavit was filed in one of 13 libel lawsuits brought against Singapore opposition politician Tang Liang Hong after elections in January.
Malaysia on Wednesday officially asked Lee to apologise and retract the statement.
"If the senior minister really values our good will, he should retract his statement and tender an apology," Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said in a statement.
